our_title: 64-bit Gnum build: element bit array of meshInduceSepa uses 32-bit words with INTSIZEBITS indexing
ran:
LD_LIBRARY_PATH=build64/lib; mmk_m2 32 32 m.msh; mord m.msh /dev/null -vt
mesh_induce_sepa.c:160:45: runtime error: shift exponent 32 is too large for 32-bit type 'unsigned int'
hmesh_order_gp.c:145:22: runtime error: pointer index expression ... overflowed
AddressSanitizer: SEGV on unknown address (pc in _SCOTCHhmeshOrderGp) ; also repro/SEP-02 sep02_64 32 0 0 and 64 0 1 (unweighted meshes). Patched 64-bit: ok; check_prog_mmk/gmk_msh/mord extended with the 32x32 mesh pass on both builds.
evidence: `unsigned int * restrict       orgbitstab;` ... `orgbitssiz = (orgmeshptr->velmnbr + (INTSIZEBITS - 1)) / INTSIZEBITS;` ... `orgvelmbit  = orgvelmidx & (INTSIZEBITS - 1); orgvelmidx /= INTSIZEBITS; indvelmnbr += (orgbitstab[orgvelmidx] >> orgvelmbit) & 1; orgbitstab[orgvelmidx] &= ~(1U << orgvelmbit);` with INTSIZEBITS == 64 in -DINTSIZE64 builds: elements k and k+32 of a 64-element block share a bit, indvelmnbr is undercounted, the induced mesh arrays are too small. Introduced long ago; 7.0.17's 6a00c51 only changed `1 <<` to `1U <<` on this line.

fix_options.label: UINT words (committed)
fix_options.summary: Declare the bit array as UINT, whose width is INTSIZEBITS by definition (common.h:274,277), and shift (UINT) 1.
fix_options.tested: mord/sep02 on 32x32 and 64x64 meshes, 32- and 64-bit builds; check_prog_mmk/gmk_msh/mord/mesh_order on both.
fix_options.maintainer_fit: Minimal and consistent with common.h's own `(UINT) 1 << (INTSIZEBITS - 1)`; same shape as his 6a00c51 bit-set fixes.

fix_options.label: Keep unsigned int, index with its own width
fix_options.summary: Replace INTSIZEBITS by (sizeof (unsigned int) << 3) as library_dgraph_map_stat.c:189,432 does.
fix_options.tradeoffs: Longer expressions repeated three times; same result.
fix_options.maintainer_fit: He used that idiom once in library_dgraph_map_stat.c, but here the INTSIZEBITS macro is already in place, so changing the word type is the smaller diff.

our_title: hmeshInducePart re-allocates its edge array unchecked and returns success with a NULL edge array
ran: SCOTCH_PTHREAD_NUMBER=1 ./common/failscan.sh ./SEP-03/sep03_err 300 1 (patched lib): 6 runs 'hmesh_induce.c:363:25: runtime error: applying non-zero offset 18446744073709551612 to null pointer' right after the injected failure, then crashes in meshCoarsenMatchNg / hmeshHgraph:185 on the NULL edge array; with mesh base 0 (sep02 scans) the same failure is silent and shows up as 'load of null pointer' in mesh_coarsen.c and SEGV in hmeshHgraph.
evidence:
`indmeshptr->m.edgetax  = memRealloc (indedgetax + indmeshptr->m.baseval, indmeshptr->m.edgenbr * sizeof (Gnum));
  indmeshptr->m.edgetax -= indmeshptr->m.baseval;` (no NULL test; routine returns 0 afterwards)

fix_options.label: Check the re-allocation
fix_options.summary: Test the result; on failure free the group leader, hmeshExit the induced mesh and return 1.
fix_options.tested: compiled only; not applied to the series because hmesh_induce.c is outside this group's files (G11 owns the hmesh family).
fix_options.maintainer_fit: Same shape as mesh_induce_sepa.c:338-343 (his own checked memRealloc).

our_title: hmeshOrderCp re-uses the element load array with the fine element base for a re-based compressed mesh
read_only: hmesh_order_cp.c:193-209: coarmeshdat.m.velmbas = baseval but velotax is copied as is; for a mesh whose nodes come first (velmbas > vnodbas, allowed by SCOTCH_meshBuild and mesh files) the compressed mesh reads velotax[coarvelmnum] with the wrong base; for file meshes the single load array keeps it in bounds (wrong values), for SCOTCH_meshBuild meshes with a separate element load array it reads before the array.
why_not_run: Needs a nodes-first mesh with element loads; the harnesses build elements first. Not run for lack of time; the fix is a one-line base shift.
evidence: `coarmeshdat.m.velotax = finemeshptr->m.velotax; /* Re-use element vertex load array, if any */` while `coarmeshdat.m.velmbas = coarmeshdat.m.baseval;` (:193) and edges are shifted by `(finemeshptr->m.velmbas - coarmeshdat.m.velmbas)` (:352)

fix_options.label: Shift the array by the base difference
fix_options.summary: velotax + (fine velmbas - coarse velmbas), NULL if absent.
fix_options.maintainer_fit: Mirrors the edge index shift at :352.

our_title: bgraphBipartFm frees its tables on resize failure and keeps running on them
read_only: bgraph_bipart_fm.c:598-605: on `bgraphBipartFmResize (...) != 0` it prints, frees hashtab and the gain table, then falls through to `for (hashnum = ...; hashtab[hashnum].vertnum != ~0; ...)` and continues the pass: use after free.
why_not_run: Needs an allocation failure inside the bipartitioning resize; outside this group's files (bgraph family), so only reported.

fix_options.label: Return after freeing
fix_options.maintainer_fit: Same as kgraph_map_fm.c:1098-1103, which returns after freeing.

our_title: vmeshSeparateFm save array holds hashmax records while a sweep can save one per element and per node
ran: Patched tree with the resize completed but the old sizing, vmesh_separate_fm.o built with -DSCOTCH_DEBUG_VMESH2/3 (tables estimate / 8): mord m2_32_32.msh -> AddressSanitizer: heap-buffer-overflow WRITE of size 4 ... _SCOTCHvmeshSeparateFm vmesh_separate_fm.c:707 (movetab[savenbr].data.node.vertpart). Sized to 2 * hashmax: all forced-resize runs clean (repro/PS-SEP-2/dbg_forced_results.txt).
read_only: In pristine the 4x shield keeps both tables sparse; the window (helmnbr + hnodnbr > hashmax before either reaches hashmax) still exists for very large meshes.
evidence: `&movetab, (size_t) (hashmax * sizeof (VmeshSeparateFmSave)), NULL)` while records are appended for elements (:605-611, :829-835) and nodes (:682-686) up to one per slot in use, resize at `helmnbr >= hashmax` / `hnodnbr >= hashmax`

fix_options.label: Size for both tables (committed)
fix_options.summary: 2 * hashmax records, in the allocation and in the resize.
fix_options.tested: forced-resize debug runs on four meshes; full check set on both trees.
fix_options.tradeoffs: Twice the save array memory (small next to the hash tables).
fix_options.maintainer_fit: Part of finishing the resize; vgraph sizes its save array to hashsiz for the same reason.

fix_options.label: orderExit on the error path
fix_options.summary: Call orderExit (&coarordedat) before hmeshExit in that block.
fix_options.tested: untested: not written as a diff, outside this group's files; two-line change

our_title: meshCoarsen sets the coarse mesh flags with a Graph constant and never checks its final re-allocation
read_only: mesh_coarsen.c:136 `coarmeshptr->flagval = GRAPHFREEVERT;` (same value as MESHFREEVERT, wrong family); :334 `coarverttax = memRealloc (...)` unchecked then re-based.
why_not_run: Fixed in passing in patch 0004; the realloc path was covered by the sep03 fault-injection scan (no finding).
evidence:
`coarmeshptr->flagval = GRAPHFREEVERT;` ; `coarverttax = memRealloc (coarverttax + coarmeshptr->baseval, (coaredgeoftval + coarmeshptr->edgenbr) * sizeof (Gnum)); /* Re-allocate array to save space */
  coarmeshptr->verttax = coarverttax - coarmeshptr->baseval;`

fix_options.label: Fixed in the SEP-03 commit
fix_options.summary: MESHFREEVERT; checked memRealloc with out of memory (3) and cleanup.
